M7E.5B.2 — fixed-schema automatic course demonstration (NOT COMMISSIONED)

Scope and current gate
----------------------
The existing push → tests/scans → build once → verified immutable S3 publication
→ deploy-production flow is retained. Production execution is still the literal
"false" in ci.yml; deployment-policy.json still has commissioned=false and no
approval/contract. Do not enable either flag to bypass missing evidence.
Brief API downtime and explicit manual recovery are acceptable. No migrations,
database recreation, volume deletion, automatic rollback or HA machinery is added.

Fixed demonstration contract
-----------------------------
The reviewed policy must contain schema_version=1, commissioned=true, an approval
object with reviewer/review_reference, and contract fields:
  id, baseline_release_id, no_database_changes=true
  schema_sha256, postgres_image (the exact existing digest-pinned PostgreSQL image)
  database_service_sha256, networks_sha256, volumes_sha256
  live_schema_sha256 (reviewed EC2 measurement, NOT inferred from init SQL)
  checker_sha256 (scripts/demo_compatibility.py)
  dependency_sha256: an exact map for these four reviewed files:
    app/__init__.py, app/version.py, scripts/release.py, scripts/ssm_deploy.py
  required_checks, exactly in this order:
    package_contract, image_identity, startup_health, existing_record,
    checkout_replay_persistence, startup_recovery, schema_unchanged

No approved values are fabricated by the repository. Hash the exact reviewed
bytes; the inline seed fixtures are covered by the checker hash. The checker
verifies its local import closure before importing it. A scripts/__init__.py is
not supported without expanding and reviewing that closure. No third-party
Python dependencies are required by the checker or host bootstrap.

contract_facts() in ssm_deploy.py hashes normalized database/network/volume
configuration. Only credential values, the package-relative schema source,
omitted defaults and the known Compose dollar-escaping difference in the database
health probe are normalized. Review actual CI and Compose 2.40.3 outputs together.
All other database configuration changes block automatic deployment.

scripts/demo_compatibility.py --package PACKAGE --policy POLICY --output NEW_FILE
loads the exact verified candidate image (never builds it), starts UUID-owned
PostgreSQL/API resources, seeds a completed payment and an unfinished attempt,
tests startup/health, existing-record reads, checkout persistence and idempotent
replay, then checks the schema is unchanged. Startup recovery intentionally marks
unfinished attempts ERROR; this is part of the reviewed demo behavior. Cleanup
must succeed before evidence is emitted. No production data is used as a fixture.

Evidence is JSON: schema_version=1, passed=true, release_id, image_id,
policy_sha256, contract_id, live_schema_sha256 and checks mapping every required
check to boolean true. It binds the candidate to the approved policy and actual
executed assertions. It is not an independent signed attestation: reviewed branch
code, the runner and authorized SSM callers remain trusted. Source/helper changes
require review and corresponding approved hashes; ordinary API-only changes do not
require per-release manual approval. Keep workflow/checker changes review-protected.

Live preflight and M7E.5A authorization
--------------------------------------
SCHEMA_SQL in ssm_deploy.py runs one bounded READ ONLY transaction with fixed
search_path, 5s statement timeout and 2s lock timeout; Docker/psql has a 15s limit.
It inspects public.payment_attempts columns/types/nullability/defaults, constraints,
indexes, table properties, unexpected triggers/rules/RLS, and the directly required
gen_random_uuid() function and extension membership. It reads no customer rows.
This is a fixed one-table contract, not a migration/catalog-management framework.
The approved snapshot and its digest must match the live database before loading
and again immediately before API replacement. Inaccessible or changed schema fails.
Out-of-band database changes require pausing automatic deployment and reviewing
both the policy and baseline. Never automatically adopt the current live schema.

The wrapper validates policy/evidence, baseline, ordering, package, live database,
network and volume before passing the recorded current release as rollback_safe_from.
That M7E.5A argument is explicit compatibility authorization, NOT an instruction to
roll back. No M7E.5A safeguard was removed. Interrupted state and state/order mismatch
require manual recovery; resume/operations-stopped flags are never supplied here.

Ordering and truthful completion
--------------------------------
GitHub concurrency uses queue:max and cancel-in-progress:false. It preserves
waiting jobs but is not the ordering authority. The host lock and root-owned
ordering record compare workflow_id and (run_number, run_attempt):
- Higher run number with a distinct run ID: eligible after all other checks.
- Same run number, higher attempt: eligible only for the same run ID/version/commit.
- Equal order and exact same release: retry; M7E.5A revalidates actual health.
- Older order: refused as stale; no deployment success is reported.
- Conflicting identities, missing/inconsistent order or interrupted state: fail closed.
A failed build/publication cannot reach deployment. A newer failed commit does not
veto a successful earlier run: current-branch-head equality checks were removed.
Originating run/attempt, commit, approved repository/branch and successful prerequisite
jobs are still independently checked. No S3 timestamps or latest pointer are used.

The exact release ID flows through build/publish job outputs; the publication output
also pins SHA256SUMS. All five package files and the archive/image identity remain
verified. The deployer is conditionally published to releases/deployment-tools/SHA/
deploy_ec2.py, downloaded conditionally and checksum-verified, then installed root-owned
0600 under /opt/asaanpay/deployers/SHA.py. Existing matching tool bytes may be reused;
neither tool nor release objects are overwritten. Host Python needs no checkout/venv.

SSM targets only i-00fc050cde50b051e using AWS-RunShellScript. A fixed systemd unit,
bootstrap flock and M7E.5A lock prevent overlap. systemd-run --wait/--collect uses
RuntimeMaxSec=600, TimeoutStopSec=30, KillMode=control-group and SendSIGKILL=yes.
SSM execution is bounded to 720s; polling is bounded to 780s. Measure these budgets
on the target. A lost caller does not authorize another uncoordinated deployment.
SSM Success/exit 0 must also carry a nonce-bound receipt written only after health,
verified release state and ordering are recorded. A timeout/uncertain submission
is not retried automatically. Failure can require manual inspection; no automatic
rollback is enabled. Logs must not include production.env or raw credential output.

Ordered commissioning checklist — NOT EXECUTED BY THIS IMPLEMENTATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. LOCAL REVIEW/TEST: Review checker/helpers, fixed schema and the intended baseline.
   Run Python tests, the workflow guard tests and actionlint/ShellCheck/Bandit.
   actionlint 1.7.12 lacks concurrency.queue support (upstream issue #657). Its only
   expected diagnostic is unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency". Validate queue=max
   and cancel-in-progress=false with the strict workflow tests, then run actionlint
   with only that exact diagnostic ignored. Do not ignore other syntax diagnostics.
2. READ-ONLY AWS: Verify account 642195693459/us-east-1, exact branch OIDC trust,
   target SSM Online/Linux status and attached AsaanPay-EC2-Role. Review existing
   permissions; never add broad grants. GitHub needs S3 GetObject for releases/*,
   PutObject for releases/deployment-tools/*, SendCommand for the exact instance and
   AWS-RunShellScript document, GetCommandInvocation and DescribeInstanceInformation.
   The latter two read actions need Resource=* with regional restriction. EC2 needs
   GetObject for release/tool keys and existing SSM access. Inspect any KMS conditions.
3. READ-ONLY EC2 PAYLOAD: uname -m; cat /etc/os-release; /usr/bin/python3 --version;
   aws --version; sudo docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}';
   sudo docker compose version --short; systemd-run --version.
   Require AL2023/x86_64, Python 3.9, Docker 25, Compose 2.40.3; inspect disk headroom,
   root ownership/permissions and existing database/image/volume/network identities.
   Do not print environment files or full container Env. Sending even read-only
   payloads through SSM creates AWS command state and needs authorization.
4. ARTIFACT CHECK: Select an explicit successful CI release, verify the same-run
   artifact and S3 marker/all five files, and test its actual Docker-save format on
   the approved runtime. Downloads write local files; Docker load writes daemon
   storage. Use disposable resources, never replace production during this check.
5. BASELINE MEASUREMENT/REVIEW: Export the reviewed SCHEMA_SQL locally; run it via
   psql -X -q -A -t -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 on the existing database with its existing
   POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_DB. Capture catalog JSON without credentials. Compare it
   with the disposable approved-schema snapshot and review it before approving
   schema_digest(snapshot). Record actual full database ID, volume Name/Driver/
   Options/Mountpoint/CreatedAt, network inspect minus Containers/Peers, and order.
6. CONTROLLED HOST INSTALLATION (MODIFIES HOST): Approve policy and baseline files.
   Install root:root 0600 as /opt/asaanpay/config/deployment-policy.json and
   deployment-baseline.json; preserve production.env and existing resources.
   Baseline fields: schema_version=1, approval={reviewer,review_reference},
   policy_sha256, baseline_release_id, live_schema (reviewed snapshot),
   database_container_id, volume, network, order={workflow_id,run_number,
   run_attempt,release_id}. For explicitly approved adoption with no deployment
   state use release_id=null/run_number=0/run_attempt=0 and actual workflow_id.
   Existing state requires reconciled matching order, not a fabricated zero reset.
7. DISPOSABLE SUPERVISION TEST (MODIFIES HOST/AWS STATE): With approval, test SSM/
   systemd success, nonzero exit, timeout and caller interruption in test-only units.
   Confirm descendant cleanup and missing-receipt failure. Never invoke production
   deployment merely to test supervision. Preserve root-owned diagnostic evidence.
8. FIRST LIVE AUTHORIZATION: Approve the enablement commit/first successful run,
   short downtime and manual recovery procedure. Set commissioned=true in the
   reviewed host-matched policy and the literal execution gate to "true". Update
   the static test's uncommissioned-state expectation as part of that review.
9. DEMONSTRATE SUCCESS: A Git push passes tests/scans, publishes, automatically
   deploys that exact release, and reports verified health/SSM receipt. Through the
   existing browser ingress/proxy verify version/commit and a simulated payment.
   Keep API loopback binding and PostgreSQL private; commission browser ingress
   separately only if missing. Confirm existing records and DB container/network/
   volume identities are unchanged (apart from approved unfinished-attempt recovery).
10. DEMONSTRATE FAILURE: A deliberately failing CI check must produce no deployment.
    Compare recorded release/API identity before/after. No cleanup may delete the
    production database volume. There are no per-release approvals after commissioning.

References: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency
https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/657
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_ssm.html
